message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know or dive deeper into any part that interests you.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| **1** | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office work) and how much you’re willing to spend. | Use online PC builders (e.g., PCPartPicker) to compare prices and check compatibility. |
| **2** | **Choose a Case** | Houses all components; determines airflow, size, and aesthetics. | Pick ATX, Micro‑ATX, or Mini‑ITX depending on motherboard size. |
| **3** | **Pick a Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to everything; must be reliable and efficient. | Look for 80+ Bronze or better, 80+ Gold if you’re serious. Get 10–15% headroom over your estimated wattage. |
| **4** | **Select a Motherboard** | Connects CPU, RAM, storage, GPU, and peripherals. | Match the socket to your CPU (e.g., LGA 1200 for Intel 10th‑gen). Check BIOS support for your chosen CPU. |
| **5** | **Get a CPU** | The brain of the PC. | Consider performance per dollar: AMD Ryzen 5/7 or Intel Core i5/i7. |
| **6** | **Add RAM** | Determines multitasking ability. | DDR4 or DDR5, 16 GB minimum for gaming, 32 GB+ for content creation. |
| **7** | **Choose Storage** | SSDs are fast; HDDs are cheap for bulk. | NVMe M.2 SSD for OS + games; SATA SSD/HDD for extra space. |
| **8** | **Install a Graphics Card (GPU)** | Needed for gaming, 3D rendering, or GPU‑accelerated tasks. | Ensure PSU has enough wattage and the case has enough clearance. |
| **9** | **Prepare the Case** | Clean, remove panels, install standoffs. | Keep a small screwdriver set handy. |
| **10** | **Mount the Motherboard** | Align with standoffs and screw it in. | Double‑check that all standoffs are correctly placed. |
| **11** | **Install the CPU** | Insert into socket, secure, apply thermal paste. | Follow the motherboard manual for the correct orientation. |
| **12** | **Attach the CPU Cooler** | Keeps the CPU from overheating. | Stock coolers are fine for most CPUs; aftermarket coolers give better cooling and quieter operation. |
| **13** | **Insert RAM** | Slot into DIMM slots. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel mode. |
| **14** | **Mount Storage** | Secure SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot. | Use screws or tool‑free mounting brackets. |
| **15** | **Install the GPU** | Slide into the top PCI‑Express x16 slot. | Secure with screws, connect any required PCI‑e power cables. |
| **16** | **Connect Power Cables** | PSU to motherboard, GPU, drives, fans. | Label cables or keep them organized to avoid confusion later. |
| **17** | **Attach Case Fans & Front Panel Connectors** | Front USB, audio jacks, power button, reset button. | Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pinouts. |
| **18** | **Cable Management** | Tidy cables improve airflow and aesthetics. | Use zip ties, Velcro straps, or cable combs. |
| **19** | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Power on, enter BIOS, check component detection. | Update BIOS if necessary, set boot order to your SSD. |
| **20** | **Install Operating System** | Windows, Linux, or other OS. | Create a bootable USB with the OS installer. |
| **21** | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure all hardware works optimally. | Download latest drivers from manufacturer sites. |
| **22** | **Test & Benchmark** | Verify stability, temperature, performance. | Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark) and monitor temps. |
| **23** | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep drivers updated, clean dust, monitor temperatures. | Schedule regular cleaning every 3–6 months. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- [ ] Case
- [ ] PSU
- [ ] Motherboard
- [ ] CPU
- [ ] CPU cooler
- [ ] RAM
- [ ] Storage (NVMe SSD + optional HDD)
- [ ] GPU
- [ ] Case fans
- [ ] Front panel connectors
- [ ] Tools (screwdrivers, anti‑static wristband)

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **CPU not seated properly** | Re‑insert, ensure the lever clicks into place. |
| **GPU not fully inserted** | Push firmly until the latch clicks; secure with screws. |
| **Power cable mis‑connected** | Double‑check PSU manual; label cables. |
| **No display output** | Verify GPU is powered, cables are connected to GPU, not motherboard. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow, clean dust, consider better cooler. |

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build lists, price tracking, compatibility checks.
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help and advice.

Happy building! If you hit a snag or need component recommendations, just let me know.
